strengths: Novel framing of text-to-CAD as an interactive problem with proactive clarification—addressing a practically important issue of under-specified/inconsistent specifications
High-quality text-to-CadQuery dataset (10K samples) with thoughtful annotation pipeline: multi-modal conditioning (images + code), leakage/completeness checks, 80%+ automated
Strong empirical results: 79.9% reduction in mean Chamfer distance vs Claude Sonnet 4.5 on ambiguous prompts; invalidity ratio reduced from 4.8% to 0.9% using only 1.6K fine-tuning samples

Comprehensive evaluation: multiple baselines, both LLM and human evaluation, ablation studies (interaction protocols), out-of-distribution generalization tests, detailed failure analysis showing 99.4% of failures are under-clarification
Clear presentation with good motivation, informative case studies, and extensive appendices enabling reproducibility
Dataset creation pipeline avoids JSON minimalism of prior work (Text2CAD) by conditioning on CadQuery code, showing advantages in clarity and human-likeness
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on synthetic ambiguity: two types (under-specified, conflicting) generated by GPT-5-mini perturbation may not reflect real-world diversity; unknown if other ambiguity types exist in practice

Limited real-world validation: human evaluation uses only 100 examples with artificial setup (annotators provided original unambiguous prompt); no evaluation on naturally-occurring ambiguous prompts from real users
Circular evaluation dependencies: data generation and completeness checks both use GPT-5-mini, potentially biasing descriptions toward what this specific model can handle; systematic bias risk
LLM-based user simulation may not reflect real user behavior; paper assumes users provide correct answers to clarification questions, which is unvalidated assumption

Misleading framing of training efficiency: '1.6K samples' come from curated 10K dataset with 20% requiring manual expert intervention; the headline obscures data quality as the real driver of performance

Limited technical novelty: agentic SFT is standard supervised fine-tuning with JSON formatting; MDP formulation is straightforward; main contribution is application to a domain rather than methodological innovation
Narrow scope: text-to-CAD is a specialized domain with unclear transferability of insights to other interactive AI systems or ambiguity resolution problems
Insufficient analysis of synthetic ambiguity selection: CD ratio filter (≥10) is arbitrary; no ablation on realism of perturbations or their distribution compared to natural ambiguities

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Addresses genuine challenge of ambiguous CAD specifications with sensible shift toward proactive clarification

High-quality dataset contribution: Carefully constructed 10K text-to-CadQuery dataset with thoughtful reverse-direction pipeline, multi-view conditioning, systematic leakage detection, and completeness verification achieving >80% pass rate without human intervention
Impressive coding agent efficiency: Achieves competitive performance with Claude Sonnet 4.5 using only 1.6K samples versus 150K+ in prior work, suggesting exceptional dataset quality

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple metrics, comparisons with frontier models, LLM-as-judge validation with 96% human agreement, interaction protocol ablations, and detailed failure mode analysis
Thorough documentation: Extensive appendices with case studies, failure modes, complete system prompts, and supplementary analysis supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in clarification agent: Uses standard supervised fine-tuning on synthetic trajectories with no novel algorithmic contributions; reduces to straightforward JSON output task; applies existing techniques to new domain rather than advancing methodology

Unrealistic and circular user simulation: Uses GPT-5-mini to both generate ambiguous prompts and simulate user responses, creating self-validating loops; assumes users always provide correct answers to clear questions—unrealistic in practice; only 100 manual examples in human evaluation; no real user studies despite this being critical for validating interactive systems

Unfair baseline comparisons: Compares fine-tuned clarification agent against untrained single-model baselines (Claude, GPT-4o-mini) not designed for interactive clarification; doesn't compare against other clarification-designed systems or interactive refinement methods mentioned but not evaluated

Synthetic ambiguity may not reflect real patterns: Only two ambiguity types (under-specified, conflicting); perturbation-based generation via LLM; arbitrary filtering criteria; ~40% discard rate suggests potential selection bias; large gap between synthetic and natural ambiguities in real engineering specifications

Fundamental limitations revealed in failure modes (Appendix J): 99.4% of failures from asking too few questions (not too many); single-ambiguity success 98.2% but sharp drop to 77.1% for dual ambiguities; authors acknowledge 'translating answered information back into corrected prompt remains nontrivial'; suggests approach may not scale to complex specifications

Modest empirical improvements on core task: Mean CD improvement 3.10→0.85; invalidity 4.8%→0.9% (baseline already reasonable); when coding=Claude, gains smaller; unclear if two-agent complexity justified by improvements; gains may be attributable to fine-tuning rather than clarification strategy

Statistical rigor lacking: No confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; no indication of variance across runs; human evaluation limited to 100 examples without statistical testing; all results presented as point estimates

Dataset realism concerns: Descriptions synthetically generated by VLMs rather than written by humans; may not reflect natural user language patterns or typical ambiguities; LLM-judge comparisons (Table 3) against Text2CAD suffer from acknowledged position bias; generalization to other CAD representations unknown
Incomplete reproducibility: Abstract claims code/datasets 'made publicly available' but no URL provided in manuscript; implementation details incomplete despite lengthy appendix

Unfair treatment of baselines: Single-model baselines not designed for interactive tasks; no comparison against clarification-specific dialogue systems adapted to this domain; doesn't isolate value of clarification from value of fine-tuning

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real ambiguity issues in CAD specifications
High-quality curated 10K text-to-CadQuery dataset with multi-stage verification pipeline, demonstrating that data quality exceeds scale
Efficient training achieving strong results with only 1.6K samples vs. 100K+ in prior work
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across synthetic simulators (GPT-5-mini, Claude Haiku) and human studies with expert scoring
Strong empirical results: 79.9% reduction in Chamfer distance, 0.9% invalidity ratio vs. 4.8% for Claude Sonnet 4.5
Thorough failure analysis and policy ablation studies (Appendices J, K) with honest assessment of limitations
Novel two-stage training decomposition (coding vs. clarification) with agentic SFT on synthetic trajectories
Clear presentation with reproducible methodology; code and datasets promised for release
weaknesses: Limited ambiguity scope: only two types (under-specification, conflicts) addressed; generalization to other ambiguity types unclear
Unrealistic assumption that users always provide correct answers to clarification questions; no robustness analysis for incorrect/incomplete user responses
Multi-ambiguity detection significantly weaker (77.1% success for k=2 vs. 98.2% for k=1), suggesting poor scaling to realistic prompts with multiple issues
Weak baselines for clarification agent: Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-4o-mini not designed for this task; no comparison to dialogue systems or clarification-focused methods
Human evaluation limited to 100 examples with expert annotation; no real end-user studies with actual interactive dialogue
Dataset annotation pipeline is expensive and specific to CadQuery; scalability and generalization to other CAD systems (OpenSCAD, Fusion 360, etc.) unclear
Synthetic user simulation (GPT-5-mini) may not reflect real user behavior; while OOD testing with Claude Haiku helps, the regime remains limited
Insufficient analysis of when clarification cannot help and systematic characterization of problematic shape types
Missing evaluation overhead of clarification agent on genuinely unambiguous prompts; unclear % of real-world prompts triggering unnecessary clarification
LLM-as-judge metrics somewhat artificial (question matching ignores paraphrases; resolution scale coarse at {0, 0.5, 1})
